newsitem.title: USA: Daschle says Republicans endanger budget talks.
newsitem.headline: Daschle says Republicans endanger budget talks.

text.p: Senate Minority Leader Tom Daschle said Wednesday budget negotiations would be endangered if Republicans forced passage of an automatic government spending bill that President Clinton would veto.

"That would blow it up. If the president has to veto this disaster bill I don't see any need to continue on the budget negotiations for the foreseeable future," the South Dakota Democrat told reporters.
Republicans have said they will add the controversial automatic spending bill to legislation that would give $5.5 billion in disaster relief for people in 23 states.

Republicans proposed the automatic spending bill as a method of preventing future government shutdowns. An impasse over annual government spending bills led to two government shutdowns in fiscal 1996.
The Republican bill would continue government programs at 98 percent of this year's funding if regular appropriations were not approved by the Oct. 1 start of the new fiscal year.
Daschle and other Democratic senators said the lower funding would cause automatic cuts of seven percent across the board in all but mandatory benefit programs.
The total would be $35 billion below Clinton's request for fiscal 1998 funding.

Among the changes the automatic spending cut would force were -- elimination of 1,350 medical research projects; the loss of nutrition funds each month by 700,000 mothers and children; a fall in college aid of $1.8 billion; elimination of federal crop insurance; and elimination of government computer adjustment for the year 2000.

Democrats said they expect the Republican-controlled Appropriations Committee will pass the automatic spending bill. Democrats would seek to have it removed in the full Senate, but would not prolong debate and would allow it to go to the White House quickly for the president's veto.
